conditions: Stationary homogeneous medium with one-dimensional conduction, constant positive conductivity, density and specific heat, no internal heat source or transverse heat loss; temperature sufficiently differentiable. Initial and boundary data are needed to specify a solution.

symbols.\\alpha: Thermal diffusivity, conductivity divided by volumetric heat capacity

spoken_aliases: the partial derivative of u with respect to t equals alpha times the second partial derivative of u with respect to x
the first partial derivative of temperature with respect to time equals thermal diffusivity times the second partial derivative of temperature with respect to position

evidence: For a fixed homogeneous rod with constant properties, Fourier conduction gives heat flux q=-k u_x. Local energy conservation gives rho c u_t=-q_x. Substitute the flux and divide by positive rho c to get u_t=(k/(rho c))u_xx. The coefficient has dimensions length squared per time.

Reference checked 2026-11-27: https://ocw.mit.edu/courses/18-303-linear-partial-differential-equations-fall-2006/d11b374a85c3fde55ec971fe587f8a50_heateqni.pdf (section 1.1, equations 2 and 3). Proposed maintainer approval, not independent human certification.
